title: I'm making a Plinko roguelike where the game show host is the devil. Does this concept work?
author: link1241
selftext: It's called Pegs & Prizes. You drop balls to hit each episode's quota and buy stuff between episodes to break the board even more. Still in development.

comments.author: Maple-Syrup89
comments.body:
The concept is really fun. The devil placement is a bit strange and the art style looks different than the rest of it, just like fake pixel art I guess. Also super tiny, confetti only falls on the top 1/3rd the screen, not sure why that bothers me. 

It feels like I would need to play it a bit to get a hang of it since there is so much to look at all at once, in a captivating but slightly overwhelming way. a tutorial that slowly adds things might be nice. I know its rogue like so you could just let players fail a few times, but I don't always like that approach.   My game time is limited so spending it losing over and over while I learn is a tough pill to swallow.

replies.author: link1241
replies.body: Dude you have no idea how much this feedback is helpfull to me, Esspeiclly the art problems. Ty so much :)

replies.author: Maple-Syrup89
replies.body:
No worries, its a really strong/memorable concept.  Keep working on it, I really think it has some legs. 

The art style overall is actually good, its just specifically making the assets themselves more high quality. 

I have a prototype where you are a gremlin inside a vending machine that vends almost anything, based on pulling the right knobs and levers. I haven't quite got the fun game loop yet, but the concept throws me. I love stuff with bizarre premises

comments.author: Hot_Perception_5263
comments.body: I think it’s a great concept, but it might get boring after 1–2 hours. Maybe Plinko should make up 60% of the game, with the rest being mini-games that fit the TV show theme, plus more interaction with the host. It looks good, though, and I’d buy your game when it’s done! Lmk if you need somebody to play and give you some feedback about the game
